shorts.title: Over 20 Shots at a Trapped Tsavo Lion, and It Walked Out
shorts.outro: Doug's five deaths are in the full video below.
shorts.description: In 1898 two soldiers in a lion trap fired more than twenty shots at a man-eater a few feet away and mostly hit the door; the whole story of the Tsavo lions is in the full episode.

shorts.title: The Tsavo Man-Eaters Weren't Starving, Their Teeth Say
shorts.hook: The Tsavo man-eaters didn't eat people because they were desperate.
shorts.outro: Doug's other four deaths are in the full video below.
shorts.description: A 2017 study of tooth wear suggests the Tsavo lions added people to an already varied diet rather than eating them out of desperation; watch the full episode for the rest.

shorts.title: The Second Tsavo Lion Kept Charging After Being Shot
shorts.outro: The first lion and Doug's other four deaths are in the full video below.
shorts.description: Patterson wrote that the second man-eater was hit again and again and still dropped barely five yards from him; the full episode tells how the Tsavo bridge got built.
